title: Action conformance fixture
description: Executable spec for the client-side action executor. Every Orca SDK (Flutter, Swift, Kotlin) loads these files, seeds state, runs `actions` (or `steps`) in order, and asserts the resulting state and the emitted effects. Effects are data: what the executor asked the host to do, with every Value already resolved.

event.description: Event payload available to V.event(...) while the actions run (a step's own `event` replaces it for that step).

serverResponses.description: Stubbed serverAction responses keyed by action id: {"actions": [...]} to return, or {"error": "message"} to fail with that message.

handlers.description: Names to register a recording handler under before the actions run; each call appends a handler record to the effects.

actions.description: Actions run in order with the fixture's `event` and no widget source.

steps.description: Steps run in order, each as if fired by `source` (so once can dedupe per widget and trigger) with its own `event`.

source.description: The widget and trigger that fired the action. Absent: no source, so once runs every time.

event.description: Event payload for this step, in place of the fixture-level `event`.

Effect.description: navigate {route, replace, params?} · goBack {} · showSnackbar {message, duration} · showToast {message, duration} · openUrl {url} · copyToClipboard {text} · share {text, subject?} · serverAction {id, params?} · switchTab {tabId} · openDrawer {} · debugLog {level, tag, message?, data?}

HandlerEffect.description: Record a handler registered from `handlers` appends when it runs: the name it was registered under and the raw action it received (type as sent, unresolved).
